result.area: Test rig and its honesty: tests/, tools/ (check.sh, determinism.sh, perf gate, lint_sim.sh, test framework)
result.real_depth:
The FRAMEWORK is first-rate. The WIRING around it produces false green.

PROVEN REAL BY EXPERIMENT (all reverted):

1. The determinism tripwire genuinely works. I injected a wall-clock read where wind is finalized (game/sim/climate/climate_system.gd:934). tools/determinism.sh output: "DETERMINISM BROKEN / FIRST DIVERGENCE / $.checkpoints.1000.systems.climate.heat_loss_mult a=1.15799999999999992 b=1.14100000000000001". It named the first divergent path, followed propagation into heat ($.checkpoints.1000.systems.heat.networks[1].deficit), and the metrics.csv advisory named the exact unstable columns (climate.wind, climate.heat_loss_mult). tools/determinism.sh:9-11 uses two SEPARATE processes deliberately, which is the correct call. THREE independent layers caught it: tests/p00/test_core_contracts.gd:349 and :354, tests/p00/test_scenarios.gd:249, and climate_test_suite replay_determinism (3 assertions).

2. tests/p00/test_core_contracts.gd:363-371 is the inverse guard, asserting two different seeds DO produce different worlds. That single test is what separates a real determinism rig from a vacuous one.

3. tests/p00/test_framework_self.gd (344 lines) makes the framework prove its own assertions fail when they should: :102 all failures recorded not just the first, :192 assert_deterministic catches drift and names the path, :152 assert_throws fails when nothing went wrong, :109 the failure record blames the author file:line not tests/framework/*. Not a tautology farm.

4. tools/perf_report.gd produces real numbers and really fails. Setting floor_multiplier to 10.0 gave: "stress_1000 3000 20210 148 7x 1000 regressed - 148 ticks/s is below the floor of 1000 / PERF REGRESSION". Pointing --runs at a missing directory gave status "error - no readable state.json ... did the run crash?". The floor lives in the scenario (expects.min_ticks_per_second), not in the gate, so a scenario cannot drift from its perf contract (perf_report.gd:9-11,113-116).

5. tools/lint_sim.sh has 8 real regex rules with a FATAL/ADVISORY split and a "# lint:allow" escape hatch. It flagged my injected Time.get_ticks_usec() as an advisory with the correct reasoning.

6. tools/parse_check.gd load()s every .gd under game/tests/tools in one engine start and returns 1 on any failure. Honest.

7. tests/framework/json_canon.gd (322 lines) is a real comparison engine: key-sorted canonical text for assertions, exact() full-precision JSON for replay hashing, diff() with epsilon and 17-digit output so a divergence in the 15th decimal is visible (json_canon.gd:309-316). Integer dict keys are zero-padded so 2 sorts before 10 (:187).

8. tests/build/test_build.gd has 371 real checks and does catch regressions: disabling the buildability check (build_system.gd:927) turned it red ("TESTS FAILED - 1 of 371 checks"). It just never runs in the gate (see hollow #1).
hollow: tools/check.sh:106-118 runs standalone suites with `--script`, which cannot compile a script referencing autoloads. tests/build/test_build.gd dies with 'SCRIPT ERROR: Compile Error: Identifier not found: Log' at test_build.gd:18, Godot exits 0, check.sh only greps for 'TESTS FAILED', finds nothing, and prints a green tick. Verified: `--script tests/build/test_build.gd` -> exit 0, zero assertions run, check.sh reports 'tests/build/test_build.gd pass'. Run via res://tests/build/test_build.tscn it actually executes 371 checks. So the ONLY suite covering 3355 lines of build system is reported green while never executing.

Test discovery (tests/framework/test_runner.gd:68) requires the filename to start with `test_`. tests/grid/grid_tests.gd (655 lines), tests/climate/climate_test_suite.gd (666), tests/camera/camera_tests.gd (749), tests/camera/camera_node_tests.gd (410) are never discovered. `--list` returns exactly 4 files. About 2480 lines of test code is invisible to the gate, and it is hiding 17 real failures (see broken).
tests/heat/ is an EMPTY DIRECTORY. 2468 lines of heat system, the game's central resource per the pitch, with zero tests of any kind.
tests/render/ contains only bake_sheet.gd, an asset generator. 4559 lines of game/view/render with zero tests.

No golden/regression baseline exists anywhere. .gitignore excludes artifacts/ and `git ls-files | grep -iE 'golden|baseline|snapshot|expected'` returns nothing. Determinism compares two runs of the SAME build, so it cannot see a behavioural regression. Proven: I halved all heat supply (heat_system.gd:154, `_total_supply += net.supply * 0.5`) and check.sh output was identical apart from the pre-existing failure. The determinism state hash silently moved from 986b84e290daadd3 to c13ebf7937bb34a9 and nothing compared it to anything. ARCHITECTURE.md:115 promises 'balance regressions show up as a diff instead of a vibe'; there is nothing to diff against.

The `expects.max_errors: 0` gate and the harness exit code are structurally dead. game/core/harness.gd:123-125 only counts Bus.alert_raised with severity >= 2, and nothing in the codebase ever emits >= 2: heat_system.gd:54 SEV_WARN = 1, climate_defs.gd:55 MAX_BUS_SEVERITY = 1, build_system.gd:208,685 emit 0/1, grid_system.gd:96 emits 1. harness.gd:100 `quit(1 if _errors.size() > 0 else 0)` can never return 1 in the current build. A Log.error inside a sim system (5 call sites exist) has zero effect on the run gate, and nothing greps the log.txt the harness writes.

The perf gate measures a fictional workload. stress_1000.json describes 'Over a thousand buildings and a thousand hostiles on one map'. The actual final state (artifacts/perf/stress_1000/state.json, artifacts/perf.json) is 350 buildings, 0 hostiles (threat is not built), and build.rejected_total 67 placements silently refused. The 148 ticks/s that passes the 100 floor is measured on roughly a third of the advertised city with no combat at all, and nothing surfaces the 67 rejections or the missing enemies.
broken: tools/check.sh is RED right now. Verified: `bash tools/check.sh` -> 'CHECK RED', exit 1. Cause is a bug in the test itself, not the data: tests/p00/test_scenarios.gd:178 asserts `shot_name == shot_name.to_snake_case().to_lower()`, but Godot 4 to_snake_case() inserts an underscore before a digit run, so 'p13_dawn_wide' becomes 'p_13_dawn_wide'. Six assertion failures against six perfectly valid shot names in smoke.json.

The undiscovered grid suite has 9 real failures. `--script tests/grid/run_grid_tests.gd` -> 'grid: 415 passed, 9 failed / TESTS FAILED'. Including: '10 tiles straight costs 10 moves: got 1000, expected 100', 'incremental repair matches a from-scratch rebuild after every change: got 55, expected 0', 'footprint on the border ridge is refused', 'a blizzard queues no pathfinding work at all: got 1, expected 0', 'a wall has no speed'. None of this reaches check.sh.

The undiscovered camera suite has 8 real failures. `res://tests/camera/run_camera_tests.tscn` -> 'TESTS FAILED - 522 checks, 8 failures'. Including: 'wheel_zoom_anchors_on_cursor: wheel zoom did not anchor on the cursor ((902.4122, 224.6955) vs (-142.1606, -342.1606))', 'middle_drag: drag moved the camera wrongly', 'bus_focus: Bus.camera_focus_requested did not start a focus move', 'keyboard_pan: holding the pan key did not move the camera east', 'box_select: box covered [P: (344, 251), S: (339, 301)], expected [P: (-18, -21), S: (12, 11)]'. Those are core camera controls, silently red.

The determinism scenario does not do what it claims. determinism.json's description says it 'Pokes every system that owns an Rng stream'. Its log (artifacts/determinism/determinism_a/log.txt) shows 7 of 25 commands dropped: 4x 'unhandled command: threat', plus society, research, logistics, citizens, and additionally 'unknown command op reveal' from grid. It reaches 4 of the 9 systems it names, and Sim._advance (game/core/sim.gd:89) logs these at WARN so no gate reacts.

tests/scenarios/_schema.json documents `reveal` in command_vocabulary.grid, but grid_system.gd:462-472 implements occupy/release/melt/snowfall and not reveal. tests/p00/test_scenarios.gd:143-161 only checks the build vocabulary hard ('the one system that is fully landed'), so a documented-but-unimplemented op passes validation and dies at runtime as a warning.

tests/framework/sim_fixture.gd:178-201: replay() returns {} when the world fails to start, so replay_diff() returns an empty diff, and every `assert_empty(diff, ...)` determinism test passes silently. If world creation ever breaks, the project's hardest rule goes green instead of red. It needs an alive/non-empty precondition.
contract_violations: ARCHITECTURE.md:164 (section 6, definition of done) 'tools/check.sh is green (parse + tests + determinism replay)' - it is not. Exit code 1, 'CHECK RED', and the two commits after the Phase A commit were made with the gate red.

ARCHITECTURE.md:162 'It has tests in tests/<part>/ that pass headlessly' - [P02] heat has an empty tests/heat/, [P13] render has no tests, [P01] grid and [P16] camera have tests that do not pass (9 and 8 failures).

ARCHITECTURE.md:115 'so balance regressions show up as a diff instead of a vibe' - no stored baseline exists, so no balance diff is possible. Demonstrated by halving all heat supply with no gate reaction.

ARCHITECTURE.md:103 lists Time.get_ticks_msec() as flatly Forbidden in game/sim/**. grid_system.gd:70,73,449,454 use it. tools/lint_sim.sh:91 downgrades this to ADVISORY and passes. In this case the values only feed profiling counters (_gen_ms, _flush_us) and determinism.sh confirms they do not reach serialize(), so the code is fine, but the lint is deliberately more lenient than the contract it claims to enforce (lint_sim.sh:2 'greps game/sim/** for the things section 3 forbids').

ARCHITECTURE.md:71 'tests/<part>/ - each part owns its own folder'. Four parts shipped suites under filenames the shared runner cannot discover (grid_tests.gd, climate_test_suite.gd, camera_tests.gd, camera_node_tests.gd) and one shipped a Node-based suite check.sh cannot execute. There is no naming contract written down anywhere, and test_runner.gd:68 enforces one silently.

OUT-OF-BAND, needs your attention: an autosave process (author 'claude <claude@local>', commits '1e47a9a autosave 13:39' and '35a38c5 autosave 13:42') is committing this repo every ~3 minutes. It captured one of my temporary mutations mid-experiment: commit 35a38c5 contains `_total_supply += net.supply * 0.5   # AUDIT_MUTATION`. The working tree is fully restored (git diff fca1e8c over game/ tools/ tests/ docs/ is empty, no AUDIT markers remain), so the next autosave reverts it, but 35a38c5 in history is mine, not a builder's.

result.real_depth:
YES, IT RENDERS. `timeout 120 Godot --path . --resolution 1920x1080 -- --harness --visual --scenario=smoke --out=artifacts/audit_vis` exits 0 and writes six 1920x1080 PNGs to artifacts/audit_vis/shots/. I opened all six. There is a real game world on screen: textured snow/rock/ice ground, a settlement of ~180 visible structures, belts, pipes, pylons, houses with lit windows, cast shadows, vignette, film grain. This is not a black screen and it is not theatre.

WHAT IS GENUINELY BUILT (file:line evidence):

1. palette.gd (309 lines) is a real, coherent colour authority. Nine interpolated day keyframes with sky/ambient/shadow_dir/shadow_len/lift/gain/sat/fog/bloom/chroma/star_amt (palette.gd:146-229), smoothstep blending (palette.gd:233-261), temperature->tint ramp (palette.gd:273), a shared flow_ramp for overlays (palette.gd:291). Locked hex anchors documented at the top. This is the best-designed file in the scope.

2. sprite_factory.gd (1170) + vector_canvas.gd (358) + noise.gd (117) is a real procedural rasteriser, not placeholder rects. `Godot --headless --script tests/render/bake_sheet.gd` -> "26 baked (1313 ms)" and artifacts/P13/art/buildings.png shows 19 archetypes with snow-capped roofs, chimneys, warm furnace slits, a lamp-topped pylon, a glowing greenhouse. Competent 2D asset work.

3. terrain_atlas.gd (373) bakes a 15-row atlas with genuinely tileable noise — every lattice lookup wrapped to period (terrain_atlas.gd:296-299) with 2px gutter padding (terrain_atlas.gd:107-112). Confirmed seamless in artifacts/P13/art/terrain_atlas.png. Per-terrain worley plate fracture for ROCK, slab joints for PAVED, ember specks for ASH_FIELD (terrain_atlas.gd:162-185).

4. terrain_renderer.gd (228) is real chunk streaming on three TileMapLayers with load budget, snow-drift rebake epsilon and unload slack. Measured, not asserted: log.txt "PERF full-map stream 256x256: 64 chunks / 65536 cells in 218.6 ms (3.42 ms/chunk, 3.336 us/cell)" and "steady state: 16 chunks / 16384 cells resident for a 1920x1080 view". This part earns its comments.

5. post_process.gdshader (85) is a real full-screen stack — chromatic split, 24-tap 3-ring bloom with warm-biased flare, ground fog, lift/gain/saturation grade, vignette, shadow-masked grain. It is visibly running: vignette and grain are both plainly present in every shot, and SimClock.seconds() (post_process.gd:80) keeps the grain deterministic.

6. art_cache.gd (76) is a working versioned disk cache: log.txt "art cache v9: 0 baked (0 ms), 28 loaded from disk (13 ms)".

7. P16's camera code is genuinely written, not stubbed: camera_rig.gd:263-274 has correct anchored-zoom maths (p1 = p0 + (a-c)*(1/z0 - 1/z1)), camera_rig.gd:226-259 has drag-velocity throw, glide, focus smootherstep, and a real 522-check test suite exists at tests/camera/. There are ZERO `pass`-body stubs and ZERO TODO/FIXME markers across all 6986 lines in scope (verified by grep).
hollow: LcnLightRig (light_rig.gd, 90 lines) NEVER LIGHTS ANYTHING. Every render log line in both the harness run and a plain game run reads '... 0 lights'. artifacts/audit_vis/log.txt and the live run both show it for 100% of frames. The stated art direction — 'a cold blue-grey world lit by small warm orange islands... warmth is *earned* by heat' (palette.gd:15-17) and 'that is why the city reads as islands of heat in the dark' (light_rig.gd:6-9) — does not happen in the built game. The entire pool of 26 PointLight2Ds, the flicker maths, the strongest-source sorting and the heat_light_color ramp are dead code today.

ROOT CAUSE, proven arithmetically: world_model.gd:605 sets `live = _heat.has_method("power_factor")` -> true (heat_system.gd:266 exists). world_model.gd:616 then does `w *= clampf(0.25 + power_factor(id)*0.85, ...)`. heat_system.gd:268 returns 0.0 for any id it does not own, and it owns NONE of the preview buildings. So w = warm * 0.25. warm comes from world_model.gd:515 `warm = sp["warm"] * 0.35` because `heat_produced` is 0 for every kind the preview places. Max sp.warm is 1.0 (sprite_factory.gd:47, generator). 1.0 * 0.35 * 0.25 = 0.0875, and world_model.gd:617 discards anything below 0.12. NO building can clear the bar. Lights are off by construction, not by accident.

The 'day cycle' the palette is built around never runs. artifacts/audit_vis/metrics.csv over all 600 ticks: climate.phase is 'dawn' for every sample, climate.light goes 0.001 -> 0.101, climate.seconds_to_night stays ~300. Measured mean RGB of the six shots (all blue-dominant, mean luminance 28-78/255): dawn_wide 30/39/63, morning_industry 33/43/68, afternoon_housing 36/45/72, dusk_city 45/57/91, night_perimeter 57/72/114, night_zoomout 56/71/111. The frames named 'night' are the BRIGHTEST in the set and the frames named 'morning'/'afternoon' are the darkest. The gorgeous noon keyframe (palette.gd:185-192, sky 0.925/0.950/0.995) has never once been rendered.

The shot names in tests/scenarios/smoke.json ('p13_dusk_city', 'p13_night_perimeter') are fiction. The sim is in phase 'dawn' at every one of those ticks. Anyone reading the artifact filenames would conclude the day/night grade was verified. It was not.

The renderer logs 'world ready: 337 structures, 0 agents, source=sim' (world_renderer.gd:118-121) two lines after WARNing that all 337 are placeholders. `using_preview()` (world_model.gd:192) returns `_grid == null`, which is about TERRAIN, so it reports 'sim' while the entire visible city is synthetic. The one log line a reviewer would trust to tell them what they are looking at is wrong.

world_renderer.gd:337-346 logs 'frame %.2f ms' from `_frame_us_avg`, which times only `_process` and excludes the deferred `_draw`. In artifacts/audit_vis/log.txt that number decays monotonically 185 -> 0.35 ms while the real entity draw sits at a flat 30-32 ms in the same line. The build self-reports a frame cost ~90x better than the cost it measures on the very same line.

tests/render/ contains no tests. Its only file is bake_sheet.gd, which `extends SceneTree` and writes contact sheets — a tooling script with no assertions and no pass/fail. P13 has zero automated verification of anything: not the palette, not the grade interpolation, not the atlas seams, not the streaming, not a single pixel.
broken: THE CITY RENDERS AS A BLACK HOLE. Every wide shot (artifacts/audit_vis/shots/p13_dawn_wide.png, p13_dusk_city.png, p13_night_zoomout.png) shows a solid near-black disc ~33 tiles across swallowing the entire settlement. Sampled pixels: disc centre RGB (24,28,39), snow outside (67,85,135) — the city is 3-5x darker than the empty plain around it. Roads, walls, the turret ring, the belt spine and 46 citizens are all invisible inside it. Cause: terrain_renderer.gd:150-152 applies the soot decal as a BINARY switch at `if s > 0.22` — full-strength or nothing, no proportional blend — and the soot tile is LcnPalette.ASH at alpha 0.82 (terrain_atlas.gd:256-264), i.e. near-opaque black. Meanwhile world_model.gd:535 gives every industrial building a soot radius of `max(tiles) * 32 * 3.0` (15 tiles for a 5x5) and world_model.gd:443-449 SUMS contributions from all of them. Eight industrial buildings clustered together push soot over 0.22 across the whole settlement footprint. This is the single most damaging thing in the build and it directly negates design north star #1, 'Legible. A player must be able to look at a base and *read* it.'

P16'S CAMERA IS NOT IN THE SHIPPING GAME. `grep -rn GameCamera game/ tools/ --include=*.gd --include=*.tscn --include=*.tres` outside game/view/camera/ returns NOTHING. game/view/camera/game_camera.tscn is referenced by exactly one file: itself. game/content/view/ holds only render_bootstrap.tres — P13 gave itself a Registry-scanned self-installer (view_bootstrap.gd) and P16 did not. A plain `Godot --path .` run logs: '[INFO][render] no camera in the scene — using the render fallback camera'. The player therefore gets world_renderer.gd:282-289, a bare Camera2D with no input handling, parked at the city centre at zoom 1.0 forever (`_drive_tour_camera` returns immediately unless Harness.visual, world_renderer.gd:306). project.godot has no [input] section, and keybinds.gd:36-42 registers all InputMap actions at runtime from GameCamera, which never loads. The result: THE GAME CANNOT BE PANNED OR ZOOMED. ~2000 lines of P16 (game_camera 612, keybinds 520, camera_rig 393, selection_controller 198, selection_overlay 127, camera_shake 106, camera_tuning 129, sim_entity_provider 94) is unreachable from boot.tscn.

THE P16 TEST SUITE IS RED AND NOBODY SEES IT. `Godot --headless --path . res://tests/camera/run_camera_tests.tscn` exits 8 with 'TESTS FAILED — 522 checks, 8 failures': wheel_zoom_anchors_on_cursor (twice — got (902.4,224.7), expected (-142.2,-342.2)), middle_drag ('drag moved the camera wrongly (-3002.16,-1802.16) vs (-102.16,-62.16)' — off by ~30x), bus_focus ('Bus.camera_focus_requested did not start a focus move' and 'Bus focus never arrived'), box_select (got [P:(344,251) S:(339,301)], expected [P:(-18,-21) S:(12,11)]), keyboard_pan ('holding the pan key did not move the camera east'), and test_zoom_converges ('zoom has not settled after 0.5 s, 1.714308 vs 1.716007'). That last one is in the PURE-MATHS suite with no display server involved, so it is not a headless artifact. These are the core camera feel properties: anchored wheel zoom, middle-drag pan, and focus-on-alert.

THOSE FAILURES ARE INVISIBLE TO THE GATE, THREE WAYS. (a) `tests/run_tests.gd -- --list-standalone` returns only `res://tests/build/test_build.gd`; the camera suite is not discovered, so tools/check.sh stage 4b never runs it. (b) run_camera_tests.gd `extends Node`, so if it WERE run the way stage 4b runs standalone suites (`--script "$rel"`, check.sh:120) it prints nothing and exits 0 — a silent false green. I reproduced this: `--script tests/camera/run_camera_tests.gd` -> zero output, EXIT=0. (c) Its own docstring (run_camera_tests.gd:4) gives the wrong path, 'run_camera_tests.gd.tscn', which does not exist.

tools/check.sh --fast is RED, and the failing test is P13's own: tests/p00/test_scenarios.gd:178 rejects all six shot names — "smoke: shot name 'p13_dusk_city' must be lower_snake_case, expected 'p_13_dusk_city'". Six failures from one test. ARCHITECTURE.md §6.4 ('tools/check.sh is green') is not met, and P13 is the reason.

MEASURED SCALING WALL IN THE ENTITY PASS: ~0.18 ms of CPU per visible building. Live game at 1280x720: 'draw 13.72 ms | 73 bld 39 agents' -> 0.188 ms/building. Harness at 1920x1080: 'draw 31.16 ms | 177 bld 46 agents' -> 0.176 ms/building. Consistent across resolutions, so it is CPU-bound in GDScript, not fill-rate. At 73 entities the entity pass alone already caps the frame at ~73 fps; at 400 entities it is 72 ms/frame (14 fps). Causes: `model.heat_sources()` is rebuilt and re-allocated three times per frame (entity_renderer.gd:140, entity_renderer.gd:222, light_rig.gd:54), each walking every building and calling sprites.building(); `_visible()` recomputes `_sprite_rect` per building per pass (entity_renderer.gd:129-130) across all three passes; `_nearest_source` is O(buildings x sources) in both the shadow and the glow pass (entity_renderer.gd:164, entity_renderer.gd:248) and is currently only cheap BECAUSE the light rig is broken and sources is empty — fixing the lights will make this much worse; and entries.sort_custom with a lambda runs over every visible entity every frame (entity_renderer.gd:288). For a game whose stated bar is Factorio, this is a structural ceiling, not a tuning knob.

SHADOWS ARE HARD-EDGED GEOMETRIC SLABS, NOT SILHOUETTES. entity_renderer.gd:189-200 extrudes the axis-aligned FOOTPRINT rect, not the sprite shape, so a 1x1 pylon with lift 70 at dawn's shadow_len 2.7 throws a 189px (6-tile) hard-edged grey parallelogram with no falloff. Visible all over p13_dawn_wide.png and p13_afternoon_housing.png as large translucent bars with no object that plausibly casts them. It reads as a rendering artifact, not as light.

AGENTS ARE ILLEGIBLE. artifacts/P13/art/agents.png: the citizen/worker/soldier sprites are ~10x16px dark blobs with a single warm pixel. I upscaled 4x around the generator core in p13_afternoon_housing.png — the 46 walking citizens are indistinguishable from grain specks on the sooted ground. The log claims '46 agents' visible; a player sees none of them.

GROUND TILING READS AS A QUILT AT DISTANCE. Only 4 variants per terrain (terrain_atlas.VARIANTS = 4) each carrying a strong internal fbm gradient, selected by hash (terrain_renderer.gd:135). In p13_night_zoomout.png the snow field is a visible patchwork of alternating-tone 32px squares across the whole frame.
contract_violations: ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2 ('It has tests in tests/<part>/ that pass headlessly'): tests/render/ contains no tests at all — only bake_sheet.gd, an assertion-free contact-sheet tool. P13 has no automated verification of any kind.

ARCHITECTURE.md §6.4 ('tools/check.sh is green'): `tools/check.sh --fast` reports CHECK RED, and the sole failing test is P13's shot naming in tests/scenarios/smoke.json (test_scenarios.gd:178, six assertion failures).
ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3 ('It is visible/legible to the player'): the settlement renders as a solid black disc and the citizens render as noise. Nothing about the base is readable.

ARCHITECTURE.md §4 (artifacts contract, 'metrics.csv — per-tick series (heat, pop, hope, threat, throughput, fps)'): artifacts/audit_vis/metrics.csv has 45 columns from build/climate/grid/heat and ZERO from view. There is no fps series and no render metric. Render cost exists only as prose in log.txt, and the number it prints is the wrong number (see hollow).

ARCHITECTURE.md §5 ('No node lookups by path across parts'): world_renderer.gd:164 reaches into `terrain._loaded.erase(...)`, a private field of a sibling class, to force a rebake. Same-part so not cross-part, but it defeats terrain_renderer's own encapsulated stream/rebake contract, and a name change there breaks the renderer silently.

ARCHITECTURE.md §1 directory ownership is respected — P13 and P16 both stayed inside their folders and neither touched game/core/ or project.godot. But P16 followed the rule so literally that it never installed itself anywhere, which is why its camera is not in the game. P13 solved the same problem correctly with game/content/view/render_bootstrap.tres; P16 shipped no equivalent.

ARCHITECTURE.md §3 determinism: NOT violated by the view. LcnPreviewWorld lives under view/ and uses its own RandomNumberGenerator seeded from Rng.seed_value without touching an Rng stream (preview_world.gd:14-16, :32), so sim replay cannot be perturbed. Post-process grain and light flicker use SimClock.seconds() rather than wall time (post_process.gd:80, light_rig.gd:66). This is one contract the presentation layer genuinely honours.
ARCHITECTURE.md §5 static typing: honoured throughout. Every declaration and signature I read in all 6986 lines carries a type.
integration_gaps: CLIMATE <-> RENDER, the day/night grade never connects. climate_system.gd:178 exposes `day_progress()` and climate_system.gd:230 exposes `light_level()` whose own doc comment reads 'Render and vfx drive sky colour and shadow length off this'. world_model.gd:282 looks for methods named day_fraction / time_of_day / day_t / normalized_time. None of those exist. `grep -rn 'light_level\|day_progress' game/view/ game/ui/` returns NOTHING. So the renderer falls back to world_model.gd:285-289, a fragile PHASE_ARC heuristic that learns each phase's duration as 'the longest remaining time ever seen' (world_model.gd:314) — meaning inside a short run it pins the day to the START of whatever phase it first sampled. Two carefully written optional contracts that simply do not name the same methods.

HEAT <-> RENDER, the light contract is unimplemented. world_model.gd:597 asks for `heat_sources_for_view()`; `grep -rn heat_sources_for_view game/sim/heat/` returns nothing. The fallback path is the one that mathematically guarantees zero lights (see hollow). The optional contract documented at world_model.gd:22-24 has no implementer.

BUILD CONTENT <-> PREVIEW WORLD, the kind names do not exist. preview_world.gd:104-174 places kinds `generator_core`, `heat_plant`, `foundry`, `depot`, `mine_shaft`, `greenhouse`, `habitat`, `pylon`, `turret`, `belt`, `pipe`. game/content/buildings/ contains `coal_generator`, `the_hearth`, `smelter`, `storage_yard`, `ore_drill`, `granary`, `housing_block`, `heat_pipe`, `turret_mount`, `warmth_radiator`. Only workshop, wall and watchtower overlap, and none of those three declare heat_produced. So `_def_for()` (world_model.gd:545) returns null for essentially every placed structure, and the whole 'real footprint and real heat from the building definition' path at world_model.gd:504-520 is dead — every building silently falls back to its archetype's default size and light radius.

RENDER <-> CAMERA, no handshake exists. world_renderer.gd:271-300 politely scans the whole tree for a foreign Camera2D and stands down when it finds one — a genuinely thoughtful design. P16 never puts one there. The two parts each did their half of a protocol nobody completed. P16 needs a `game/content/view/camera_bootstrap.tres` mirroring view_bootstrap.gd, or an integrator edit to boot.tscn.

CAMERA <-> SELECTION, the duck-typed provider has no answerer. sim_entity_provider.gd:14-18 asks build/combat/production/logistics for `entity_at_world` / `entity_at_cell` / `entities_in_world_rect` / `entities_in_cell_rect`. None of the four systems that exist implement any of them, so box-select and click-select can only ever return cell coordinates. That is the documented degraded mode, so it is a gap rather than a bug — but it means the selection layer is untested against anything real.

HARNESS <-> RENDER, the shot schedule was never reconciled with the climate clock. tests/scenarios/smoke.json requests dusk and night shots at ticks 420/520/585 of a 600-tick run, but climate.seconds_to_night is still ~292 s at tick 500. No scenario in tests/scenarios/ is long enough to reach dusk, so the day grade — the largest single piece of art direction in palette.gd — has literally never been photographed.

result.area: SIMULATION — game/sim/grid, game/sim/climate, game/sim/heat, game/sim/build (independent audit: code read, build run, outputs measured)
result.real_depth:
THE HEAT SOLVER IS REAL, and it is the best thing in the repo. game/sim/heat/heat_flow.gd:390-474 is genuine max-min-fair progressive filling over three constraint families (per-tile throughput, per-source availability, per-consumer demand), with successive-shortest-path augmentation over a residual graph at heat_flow.gd:366-378 and a level-synchronous multi-source BFS router at heat_flow.gd:269-338. I did not take the comments' word for it; I drove live networks through SimFixture and measured.

  * CONSERVATION IS EXACT. Coal generator (30 u/s) against 62.9 u/s of demand: "supply_used(30.0000) - [delivered(28.2230)+loss(1.7770)+charge(0.0000)] = 0.00000".
  * DISTANCE LOSS IS REAL AND EXACT. Hearth -> 40 heat_pipes -> radiator: radiator reports dist=41, eta=0.7861. heat_pipe insulation 0.8 => loss_per_tile = 0.03*(1-0.8) = 0.006 (heat_def.gd:170-171); 0.994^40 = 0.78604. Match to 4 decimals.
  * REPEATERS ARE REAL. Booster pump at hop 22 of 44: pump eta=1.0, radiator eta=0.8813 == 0.994^21. heat_flow.gd:320-321 resets efficiency, so booster pumps are a real build decision.
  * PRIORITY SHEDDING IS EXACT. 30 u/s against 62.9 u/s: housing_block(p90) served=1.0, warmth_radiator(p85) served=1.0, turret_mount(p75)=0.0, ore_drill(p55)=0.0, workshop(p50)=0.0. Tiers built and sorted at heat_flow.gd:206-216, priorities derived from category at heat_def.gd:222-240.
  * BOTTLENECK ATTRIBUTION IS REAL. network_stats returned {"node":2000400,"kind":"geothermal_tap","reason":"supply","load":55.0,"consumers":10} and bottleneck_of() on each starved building points back at that node with kind "supply". heat_flow.gd:459-473 records the binding constraint on every consumer it choked.
  * BROWNOUT CASCADE IS REAL. heat_system.gd:648-689: 60-tick freeze hold, insulation-modified cool rate, thaw margin, frozen producer -> avail=0 (heat_flow.gd:161) -> network death. Observed 10 freezes / 0 thaws over a 72000-tick run.

HeatGraph (heat_graph.gd) is real incremental connected-components: union on add (_join:190), per-component re-split on remove (_resplit:233), plus partition_signature() so incremental and from-scratch can be compared. Deterministic tie-breaks everywhere (keys().sort() before every state-affecting iteration).

FlowField (grid/flow_field.gd:239-363) is a real Dial's-algorithm Dijkstra: 512 intrusive bucket lists, O(1) decrease-key, hand-inlined push in the hot loop, lazy seed admission so the bucket window invariant holds, corner-cut prohibition at 328-334. Full rebuild is correct (415 asserts in the grid suite pass).

ClimateSystem is real and is the most trustworthy part. Measured over a 72000-tick run: diurnal swing day 1 dawn -28.3C / afternoon -15.0C / night -25.6C; campaign cools day 1 -28.3 -> day 8 -38.6; scheduled Great Frost on day 7 peaks at -53.34C with heat_loss_mult 2.952 and that multiplier genuinely lands in heat demand (heat_flow.gd:176). Day plans rolled once per day from Rng.stream("climate") (climate_system.gd:706-745), storms schedule-driven not RNG-driven, era escalation, exposure curve, telegraphed warnings. Its own suite: 129 passed, 0 failed.

Blueprints are real data with correct algebra, verified live: signature "8x8|workshop@0,0:0|heat_pipe@5,0:0|...", rot360==original TRUE, mirror-twice==identity TRUE, JSON round-trip preserves signature TRUE. Capture rejects partially-covered buildings (build_system.gd:775), _plan_connections (build_system.gd:695) validates the stamp as a whole. Undo/redo verified working (before=4 place=5 undo=4 redo=5). Construction gating verified: ghost with an empty warehouse sits at queued=1 for 200 ticks, then completes once stock arrives.

Determinism replay genuinely passes: two separate processes, byte-identical state.json, "determinism: IDENTICAL sha256 986b84e290daadd3".
hollow: tests/heat/ IS AN EMPTY DIRECTORY. `find tests -type f` returns no heat file at all. The 2,500-line system the pitch calls 'the spine of the game' has zero tests. heat_system.gd:386 even ships invalidate_routes() with the comment 'Tests use it to prove the cached routing equals the fresh one' — no such test exists, and when I wrote it myself it FAILED (see contract_violations).

THE GATE RUNS ALMOST NOTHING. `godot --script tests/run_tests.gd -- --list` returns exactly four files: tests/build/test_build.gd and tests/p00/{test_core_contracts,test_framework_self,test_scenarios}.gd. tests/grid/grid_tests.gd (30 test funcs, 424 asserts) and tests/climate/climate_tests.gd (129 asserts) are NOT discovered — they use their own SceneTree/Node runners and check.sh never invokes them. The '79 passed, 3076 asserts' in the check.sh summary is essentially the p00 self-test plus test_build.

THE FLAGSHIP SCENARIO IS ~70% NO-OP. tests/scenarios/first_night.json calls kinds that do not exist in game/content/buildings/: 'hearth' (real id is the_hearth), 'radiator' (warmth_radiator), worker_hut, scrap_yard, stone_quarry, belt, flame_turret; plus systems citizens/production/research/society/threat that are not built. Actual log: 'command place refused: There is no building called worker_hut' x4, 'scrap_yard', 'stone_quarry', 'belt', 'hearth', 'radiator' x2. What really gets built in 1000 ticks: 2 coal generators and 10 heat pipes.

stress_1000 IS NAMED FOR TEN TIMES WHAT IT BUILDS. Its own description says 'Over a thousand buildings and a thousand hostiles on one map.' Actual final state: 350 buildings (Counter({'wall': 313, 'watchtower': 29, 'coal_generator': 8})), zero hostiles (no threat system), 37 heat networks containing 37 nodes total (i.e. every heat building is its own island, no pipe ever connected), 30 of 37 frozen, delivered 0.0. This is the ONLY scenario the perf gate measures.

economy_60min SIMULATES A DEAD CITY. Across all 360 metric rows of a 72000-tick run, heat.total_supply is 0.00 for 55 of the 60 simulated minutes and heat.deficit == heat.total_demand on every single row. 10 freezes, 0 thaws. 21 of its ~70 script commands reference buildings that do not exist. It exits 0 and writes 45 columns of impressive-looking CSV.

THE FUEL LAYER IS DEAD CODE TODAY. heat_system.gd:123 sets _fuel_autarky = true whenever logistics and production are absent (they are), so _fuel_factor returns 1.0 unconditionally (heat_flow.gd:232) and _burn_fuel returns on line 617 before doing anything. deliver_fuel/_pull_fuel/fuel_capacity/fuel_per_unit/self_burn are all inert. This one is honestly documented at heat_system.gd:121-123, so it is disclosed hollowness rather than a lie — but nothing currently exercises it.

grid op 'reveal' is called by three scenarios and does not exist: '[WARN][t000006][grid] unknown command op reveal'. The harness logs a warning and keeps going, which is exactly why a 70%-dead scenario can still report exit 0.
broken: FLOW-FIELD INCREMENTAL REPAIR IS WRONG. Reproduced from scratch, not taken from their test: clean 48x48 map, one 3x3 wall placed at (10,10), then FlowField.update(). Result: 'cells differing after ONE placement: 63 (worst delta 60)', 'e.g. cell (1, 1) live=3400 fresh=3460'. Root cause found: 'cells whose stored step cuts a wall corner (illegal move the sim would take): 2' — ILLEGAL diagonal at (12,9) dir=1 live=1980 fresh=2040, and at (9,12). game/sim/grid/flow_field.gd:187-203 only raises cells whose stored direction points AT an invalidated cell; it never invalidates a cell whose diagonal edge became illegal under the corner-cut rule that flow_field.gd:328-334 enforces on a full rebuild. So after every wall placement the field understates cost and hands units a squeeze the pathfinder itself forbids. Their own suite catches this ('incremental repair matches a from-scratch rebuild after every change: got 55, expected 0' out of 60 steps, plus 'reopened field still matches a full rebuild' FAIL and 'after 60 building changes: cells whose stored step does not match its cost: got 1') — and the gate never runs it.

PERFORMANCE IS ~1000x OFF THE STATED BAR, AND THE CAUSE IS ONE MISSING NEGATIVE CACHE. Measured with identical scenarios differing only in wall count: 4 buildings = 0.40 ms/tick (2513 ticks/s); 384 buildings = 7.52 ms/tick (133 ticks/s); 1515 buildings = 28.60 ms/tick (35 ticks/s). Perfectly linear at ~19 us per building per tick. Isolated the hot spot: 'HeatSystem._sync_from_build with 1515 buildings on the map: 28.62 ms per tick' vs 'BuildSystem.step with 1515 buildings: 0.001 ms per tick'. Isolated it further: 'HeatSystem._def_for x1515: wall (NOT a heat entity) = 28221 us | heat_pipe (cached) = 308 us -> 92x'. game/sim/heat/heat_system.gd:486-496 caches a HeatDef only on the success path; when participates() is false it returns null WITHOUT caching, so _sync_from_build (heat_system.gd:520-525) calls register_building -> _def_for for every wall/road/storage building on the map every tick, and HeatDef.from_resource (heat_def.gd:130-217) allocates a fresh object and does ~40 reflective property lookups each time. 1,515 plain walls already burn 57% of a 50 ms tick with SEVEN of the twelve sim systems not yet written.

DISABLING A PIPE DOES NOTHING. heat_flow.gd:152 sets `_cap_full[id] = d.capacity if d.conducts() else BIG` with no reference to n.enabled or n.frozen, and _route (heat_flow.gd:299-323) never checks them for conductors either. Verified live: on a hearth -> 40-pipe -> radiator run I disabled the pipe at the exact midpoint (id 1000021) and ran 100 ticks; radiator served stayed 1.0. The player-facing switch (heat_system.gd:331-339, build op set_enabled) is inert for every conduit, buffer and repeater in the game. A frozen pipe likewise keeps conducting at full throughput.

THE ROUTE CACHE IGNORES REPEATER STATE, SO THE SAME WORLD STATE GIVES TWO DIFFERENT ANSWERS. The cache key is graph version + a hash of live source ids only (heat_flow.gd:92, _source_signature:257). n.repeater_live is written at heat_flow.gd:608-609 and read by the router at heat_flow.gd:320, but flipping it never sets route_dirty. Verified live: booster pump at served=0.0 for 500 ticks while the radiator downstream still reported eta=0.8813 (boosted). Then `invalidate_routes()` + ONE tick on the identical state: eta=0.7732, pump eta 1.0 -> 0.8773, radiator served 0.427 -> 0.374. A dead booster pump keeps boosting until some unrelated event happens to dirty the route.

BLUEPRINT ROTATION SILENTLY CORRUPTS NON-ROTATABLE NON-SQUARE BUILDINGS. blueprint.gd:80-85 swaps every entry's span and increments its rot; building_def.gd:190-193 then forces rot=0 on paste for any def with rotatable=false. Two of the 21 shipped defs are non-square and non-rotatable (workshop 4x3, field_kitchen 3x2). Verified live: rotated stamp declared 'field_kitchen offset=(2,0) span=(2,3) rot=1' and 'workshop offset=(5,0) span=(3,4) rot=1'; what actually landed was 'field_kitchen at [79,50] rot=0' (3x2) and 'workshop at [82,50] rot=0' (4x3, occupying x 82-85 and spilling outside the stamp's own 8-wide bounding box). The command returned '{ok: true, placed: 9, skipped: 0}'. In a dense blueprint — the only kind worth making — this collides and silently drops entries.

WorldGrid.speed_scale RETURNS 0.28 ON A WALL. world_grid.gd:341-342: base is 0.0 for a non-walkable terrain, but the result is `clampf(base * ..., 0.28, 1.6)`, so the floor overrides it. Measured: 'speed_scale RIDGE (expect 0): 0.280 walkable=false'. Anything that multiplies movement by speed_scale will let units walk through walls at 28% pace.

WorldGrid.is_free IGNORES THE BORDER-RING INVARIANT THE WHOLE CLASS RESTS ON. world_grid.gd:221-234 checks only occupancy and the F_BUILD terrain flag; _compute_cost (world_grid.gd:317-318) hard-codes the outermost ring impassable regardless. is_free(Vector2i(0,5), 2x2) returns true on a plain map, so a building can be permitted onto a ring that is guaranteed unreachable.

THE GATE IS RED RIGHT NOW. `tools/check.sh` -> 'CHECK RED', 'tests FAIL 79 passed, 1 failed'. The failure is test_scenarios::test_shots_are_inside_the_run_and_uniquely_named rejecting the shot names 'p13_dawn_wide' etc. as not lower_snake_case (it wants 'p_13_dawn_wide'). Cosmetic, but ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.4 makes green a precondition for done, and a permanently-red gate is how the two real failures above stayed invisible.
contract_violations: ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 forbids Time.get_ticks_msec() inside game/sim/**. game/sim/grid/grid_system.gd:70, 73, 449, 454 use it. The code self-declares this ('Wall-clock is read here and NOWHERE else: it feeds metrics.csv only') and tools/lint_sim.sh classifies it ADVISORY, which is a defensible call — except that _flush_us reaches metrics() as 'path_rebuild_ms' (grid_system.gd:559), and tools/determinism.sh:76 DOES diff metrics.csv ('metrics.csv differs between the two runs. Unstable column(s)'). Today it never fires because the sampled ticks happen to have zero dirty cells (I confirmed: both replay runs emit path_rebuild_ms 0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0). It is a wall-clock column loaded into a diffed artifact, waiting for a scenario with pathfinding churn on a sample tick.
ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.2 ('It has tests in tests/<part>/ that pass headlessly'): heat has no tests at all; grid's tests exist and FAIL 9 of 424 when run by hand.
ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.4 ('tools/check.sh is green'): it is CHECK RED.

ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.5 ('A fresh critic looking at a real run cannot name an obvious hole'): three of the five shipped scenarios are majority no-ops against content that does not exist, and the perf scenario is named for 10x the entities it creates.

Determinism is PATH-DEPENDENT in two places even though the replay test passes. (a) The heat route cache above: identical physical state yields different served/eta depending on cache history, not on state. This survives replay because the cache evolves identically, but it means state.json is not a function of the world alone. (b) climate_system.gd:697-704 _ensure_plan rolls each day's weather lazily from Rng.stream('climate'); _resync_after_jump (climate_system.gd:641-659) skips intervening days after a time-jump command, so every subsequent day's weather differs from a linear run. Contained, because Great Frost days come from the profile schedule (frost_for_day) and not from the stream — the mechanically load-bearing part is safe.

ARCHITECTURE.md section 5 (static typing, doc comments, ownership) is honoured everywhere I read — this part is not theatre. Grep confirms clean on the rest of section 3: no bare randf/randi/randomize (climate and mapgen both take a RandomNumberGenerator handed down from Rng.stream), no `await` anywhere in game/sim/**, no frame `delta` (every hit is a local variable name), and only ONE unsorted .keys() iteration in the whole sim — building_def.gd:239 — which only orders a list of human-readable validation strings and touches no state.
integration_gaps: heat_system.gd:532-535 silently unregisters any heat node whose id is below LOCAL_ID_BASE (1,000,000) that BuildSystem did not report this tick. Anything that registers a heat building through the public register_building() API with a low id outside the build system is deleted on the next tick with no error. I hit this in the first probe run and it cost a full test cycle to diagnose.

The heat <-> build seam is entirely duck-typed and untested: heat calls _build.call('all_buildings'), then b.call('is_complete'), b.get('id'), b.get('kind'), b.get('cell'), b.get('rot'), b.get('enabled'), and WRITES b.set('heat_stored', ...) (heat_system.gd:504-535). The comment says 'BuildingInstance.heat_stored is documented as ours to write' — nothing enforces it, nothing tests it, and it is also the O(n-per-tick) hot path that costs the whole perf budget.

register_building returns false for non-heat kinds (heat_system.gd:220-224) and build is never told, so build re-offers every wall and road every tick forever. The two systems have no shared notion of 'this building is not yours' — that missing handshake IS the perf bug.

Scenarios address six systems that do not exist (citizens, production, research, society, threat, and grid op 'reveal'). Sim logs '[WARN] unhandled command: <system>' and continues, and the harness only fails the run on severity>=2 alerts (harness.gd:96), so a scenario can be three-quarters dead and still exit 0. There is no scenario-schema validation that a referenced building kind or system actually exists — tests/p00/test_scenarios.gd validates shot-name casing but not that the script can run.

Blueprint.total_cost() (blueprint.gd:133-140) skips entries whose kind is missing from Registry, so a stamp referencing removed content quotes a cheaper price than it charges; missing_kinds() exists but _op_place_blueprint (build_system.gd:642) never calls it before pasting.

heat_system.gd:604-612 _site_bonus reads grid.resource_amount_at for fuel-free generators, and build_world_query.gd binds to grid by method-name probing ('world query: tiles=yes bounds=in_bounds buildable=is_buildable_terrain ... names=12/7'). These probe-and-hope bindings work today but there is no test asserting any of them still resolve, so a rename in grid silently degrades heat and build to their fallback behaviour with only a DEBUG line to show for it.

result.what_a_player_now_sees: Running `godot --path .` opens on a 256x256 generated frozen plain, camera on the geothermal caldera at the centre. A settlement already stands: a 5x5 hearth with its firebox lit, heat pipes running east/west/south out of it, two warmth radiators at the ends of the runs, two housing blocks with warm lit windows, a coal generator, a workshop, a storage yard, watchtowers and a turret mount. Snow lies in drifts outside the ash floor and melts back near heat; buildings cast long shadows whose direction and length follow the sun. A HUD across the top reads the real simulation every frame: "Day 1 - Afternoon - -17 C - nightfall in 2:26", then heat delivered/demanded, deficit, loss, buffer, network count, frozen count, then the hovered cell, what is under it (with its served % and internal temperature and what choked it), and the material stock. Alerts from the sim appear in orange ("Network 3 short 8 heat/s - not enough generation"). WASD/arrows pan, the wheel zooms anchored on the cursor, middle-drag throws the map, H recentres, Space pauses, 1/2/3 set sim speed. B enters build mode: Q/E cycle the palette of everything [P11] says is placeable, R rotates, a green/red ghost validated every frame by BuildSystem.can_place() follows the cursor with the refusal reason printed in the HUD, left-click places, dragging a 1x1 piece lays a line, X demolishes, right-click/Esc exits. Every placement goes out as a Sim command, the same path a scenario uses. As the day turns, the palette grade moves through all nine keyframes: the world cools to blue, the CanvasModulate drops it dark, and the radiators and the hearth become warm islands of light with real Light2Ds and flicker on top of them. Over one first_night run the city visibly grows, a wall goes up before dusk with a heat trunk feeding the turrets, and the night is spent short of heat with buildings freezing at the perimeter.
fixes_applied: boot.gd rewritten into a real entry point: creates the world, installs WorldRenderer + GameCamera + PlayController + PlayHud, seeds an opening settlement through ordinary build commands
Renderer was never in the scene tree - add_child() on tree.root fails while the main scene is setting up and the failure was silent; it is now parented to Boot
GameCamera was unreachable from boot (P16's ~2000 lines were dead); boot installs it and gives it process_priority -50 so it applies before the renderer reads the canvas transform
Added game/play/ (integrator-owned): build mode, live ghost, line drag, demolish, selection read-out, and a 4-line HUD read straight from the sim

HeatSystem.heat_sources_for_view() implemented - the light contract world_model.gd asked for and nobody provided; lights were mathematically impossible before (max intensity 0.0875 vs a 0.12 threshold)
ClimateSystem.phase_progress() added and world_model.day_fraction() rewritten to use (phase_of_day, phase_progress); the day/night grade had literally never been rendered
HeatSystem._def_for gained a negative cache and _sync_from_build a not-ours id set - 1500 plain walls were re-deriving HeatDef from scratch every tick (28 ms of a 50 ms tick)
FlowField.update() now invalidates diagonal steps whose corner a new wall occupies; incremental repair diverged from a full rebuild on 55 of 60 placements, now 0
HeatFlow: a disabled or frozen conduit carries nothing (the player's switch was inert for every pipe, buffer and pump in the game)

HeatFlow route cache keys on every gate the router branches on (live sources, open conductors, live repeaters) instead of sources only - identical world state used to give two different answers depending on cache history
WorldGrid.is_free() honours the border-ring invariant; speed_scale() reads the cost cache so a wall no longer returns 0.28
MapGenerator places a guaranteed starter patch of every resource just inside its minimum ring
Blueprint rotation no longer swaps the span of non-rotatable buildings (workshop 4x3, field_kitchen 3x2 silently collided); place_blueprint refuses a stamp referencing missing content
grid_system no longer puts a wall-clock column (path_rebuild_ms) into metrics.csv, which determinism.sh diffs
Sim logs an ERROR for a command to an absent system; Log gained an error counter; harness gates on expects.max_errors, which was structurally unreachable before
Harness --visual quits after the last shot (--stay-open keeps the window) and waits two frames before capturing
TestRunner discovery rewritten with a written-down naming contract (test_*.gd, run_*.gd, *.tscn, scene wins over script); 2480 lines of tests hiding 17 real failures were invisible
check.sh runs .tscn suites as scenes (--script compiles before autoloads exist -> silent exit 0) and fails any suite that prints no TESTS PASSED/FAILED verdict
Fixed all 9 grid failures and all 8 camera failures (2 were genuine test bugs: push_input re-mapping mouse events through the camera under test, and edge scroll firing off a headless mouse at (0,0))

Wrote tests/heat/ from scratch: 16 behaviour tests covering conservation, distance loss, boosters, priority shedding, bottleneck attribution, the enabled switch, freeze cascade, cache-equals-fresh routing, and replay

Regenerated the whole scenario library from tools/gen_scenarios.py with real footprints and heat-connection checking; test_scenarios.gd now hard-fails on a system or a building kind this build does not have
stress_1000 rebuilt: 1717 buildings on one 1429-node heat grid (was 350 buildings, 37 single-node islands, zero connected network); perf gate enforces expects.min_buildings
SimFixture.replay_diff returns a failure instead of an empty diff when the world fails to start
BuildSystem implements entity_at_cell / entities_in_cell_rect, so P16's selection provider finally has an answerer
Soot made proportional (3 atlas levels, peak alpha 0.42 instead of a binary 0.82 stamp) and the ash terrain lightened - the settlement used to render as a solid black disc
world_renderer reports PLACEHOLDERS vs real structures honestly, and its 'frame X ms' now includes the deferred entity draw (was ~90x optimistic)

CRITICAL: .gitignore had a bare build/ which matches any depth - game/sim/build/ (3355 lines) and tests/build/ had never been committed. Anchored to /build/ and added 29 files; verified a fresh clone runs CHECK GREEN
still_hollow: PERF is the biggest one. stress_1000 runs a real 1717-building city at 46 ticks/s against its own 400 target. Profiled it: heat is 22.3 of 22.4 ms/tick, and inside heat HeatFlow._serve_tier's progressive fill is 11.3 ms. I set the floor to 35 (measured) rather than leave a 100 that a 350-building fiction used to clear. I tried removing the per-round _acc.keys().sort(); it changed which constraint binds, triggered far more residual rerouting and made the run SLOWER, so I reverted it rather than ship an unmeasured change. This is the next thing to fix and it needs a real refactor (indexed arrays instead of per-round dictionaries, or tree accumulation over the route forest).

No golden/baseline artifact exists, so ARCHITECTURE.md:115's promise that 'balance regressions show up as a diff instead of a vibe' is still unmet. Determinism compares two runs of the SAME build; halving heat supply would still pass every gate. A stored state hash per scenario is the obvious next step.
economy_60min runs clean and writes 360 metric rows but nothing gates it - perf.sh only runs stress_1000 and smoke, and no test reads its output.

Agents are still ~10x16 px blobs and there is no citizens system, so the 40 'agents' on screen are LcnPreviewWorld placeholders walking a synthetic path. They are visible at zoom 1.0 but illegible, and the log counts them as if they were real.
Ground tiling still reads as a 32px quilt when zoomed out: 4 variants per terrain, each with a strong internal gradient. Visible in every wide shot.
Shadows are still extruded axis-aligned FOOTPRINT rectangles, not sprite silhouettes, so a 1x1 pylon throws a hard-edged parallelogram with no falloff.

The fuel layer is still inert. _fuel_autarky is true while logistics and production are absent, so deliver_fuel/_burn_fuel/fuel_capacity do nothing. Honestly documented in the code, and my heat tests do not exercise it because there is nothing to exercise.
tests/render/ still has no assertions - only bake_sheet.gd. Nothing tests the palette, the grade interpolation, the atlas seams or the streaming; the visual proof is me looking at PNGs, not a gate.
The build<->heat seam is still entirely duck-typed (b.get('kind'), b.set('heat_stored')). My test asserts a wall is refused and never re-offered, but nothing pins the property names themselves.

HeatSystem still silently unregisters any node below LOCAL_ID_BASE that BuildSystem did not report this tick. Still a trap for anyone calling register_building() directly with a low id; I documented the _not_ours handshake but did not add a guard.

climate _ensure_plan is still lazy, so a time-jump command skips intervening days' weather rolls and every later day differs from a linear run. Contained (Great Frost days come from the profile schedule, not the stream) but it means state is not purely a function of tick.

The play shell is deliberately minimal: no build menu with costs, no tooltips, no research UI, no save/load. It is the difference between a tech demo and a game, not a finished UI - [P17]/[P18] replace it.

result.what_is_real:
The heat solver is not a stub in a costume, and I say that having read it line by line. `game/sim/heat/heat_flow.gd` implements level-synchronous multi-source BFS routing (fewest hops, efficiency as tiebreak, lower id as final tiebreak so it is byte-stable), max-min fair progressive filling across three constraint families (per-tile throughput, per-source availability, per-consumer demand), successive-shortest-path augmentation over the residual graph when a tile saturates with demand unmet, priority tiers so life support sheds last, repeater tiles that reset transmission efficiency to 1.0 (which is what makes booster pumps a real decision), and per-consumer bottleneck attribution with reason codes. The accounting identity in the header comment (measure at the source, flow through tile n is eta[n] * rem/eta) actually holds and keeps the solve linear. This is a deeper heat model than Frostpunk's, which is fundamentally a radius-overlap check.

Determinism is real and I verified it myself rather than trusting the gate: two separate processes, 4000 ticks, `first_night`, state.json hashed after stripping wall_ms — identical at 1aa43633da3734cb. The discipline behind it is visible and consistent: every single `.keys()` iteration in game/sim is followed by `.sort()`, in all 30-odd sites I grepped, no exceptions. `tools/lint_sim.sh` splits fatal from advisory with a `# lint:allow` escape that requires a written justification.

Climate has genuine depth: per-cell local temperature offsets, exposure curves, era progression, pre-generated day plans, Great Frosts scheduled days ahead with a four-step warning cadence carrying authored prose ("Barometers are falling across the plain. Bank every joule you can.").

The test rig is better than most shipped indies. 100 tests / 4904 asserts plus 1464 standalone checks, and check.sh explicitly treats a suite that prints no verdict as a FAILURE, with a comment recording the post-mortem where 371 build assertions were reported green while never executing. That is a team that has been burned and built the guardrail.
what_is_fake: The perf gate says PERF OK and check.sh prints CHECK GREEN while stress_1000 runs at 45.9 ticks/s against its own declared target_ticks_per_second of 400. It passes only because floor_ticks_per_second is set to 35. The scenario JSON is honest about this in prose, but the gate's exit code is not, and an exit code is what CI and future agents read.

grid.cells_repaired, grid.flow_cells and grid.tiles_dirty are 0 in all 600 metric rows and in both perf runs, while log.txt records 18 real flow repairs ('flow repair: 16 cells over 1 field(s) in 27.03 ms'). The dashboard contradicts the log, which means nobody is reading the dashboard. _flush_cells is set at grid_system.gd:460 and zeroed at :445, and the metrics sampler reads it on ticks where it has already been reset.

artifacts/critic_vis/shots/assault.png contains no assault. It is an ordinary night frame. Threat does not exist yet, which is fine and stated, but the shot name asserts a beat the build cannot produce.

The only in-world alert I saw rendered reads 'Network 5 short 0 heat/s — not enough generation'. Short by zero. heat_system.gd:807 formats a sub-1.0 deficit with %.0f. The one piece of diegetic feedback that reaches the screen is printing nonsense.

build.blueprints, build.ghosts, build.demolishing and climate.storm_intensity are pinned at 0 across all 600 rows of a 12000-tick run. Blueprints, ghosts, demolition and storms are all shipped code paths that this scenario never exercises, so the scenario is not covering the feature surface it appears to.

There is no game/ui/ directory. The entire interface is game/play/play_hud.gd, 114 lines, four Labels and a ColorRect, whose own docstring says '[P17] replaces this with the real HUD'. The build presents as further along than it is because the screenshots have atmosphere.

Every harness exit leaks: 'WARNING: 63 ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit' (99 in the visual run) and 'ERROR: 28 resources still in use at exit'. Nothing in check.sh looks at this, so an ERROR line prints on every single run and the gate still reports green.
result.visual_verdict:
Judged as a Steam page in three seconds: it would not stop a scroll, but it is not embarrassing either. dusk.png is the one frame with a real look — warm rim light on the hearth, long directional shadows, decent silhouettes, genuine sense of a cold place with a fire in it. That frame suggests someone on this project has taste.

The other six undercut it badly. midday.png is the worst: the snow is a visible grid of repeating texture tiles with hard chunk seams across the entire screen, reading as a broken texture atlas rather than terrain. The boundary between thawed ground and snow is a giant staircase of chunky axis-aligned rectangles with no blending or transition at any zoom, in every single frame. The dusk grade is applied as a flat global multiply, so the sunset tints snow 40 tiles from any light source, which reads as a color filter rather than as light.

Building variety is roughly six sprites repeated. In opening.png two structurally identical hearths sit at different scales. deep_night.png is the real indictment: state.json says 208 buildings exist, and the frame shows a black void with three white blobs. A player at deep night cannot see their own city, and deep night is the moment the entire game is named after.

Nothing in any frame communicates heat. No overlay, no network tint, no flow direction on pipes, no thermal gradient. The HUD says 'frozen 6' and I could not identify a single frozen building in any of the seven images.
result.biggest_gap: Legibility, at a 2. The premise is heat networks; the sim computes, per network, a bottlenecks array of {cell, kind, reason, load, capacity, consumers}, plus per-node dist/eta/served/bottleneck_kind, and it ships all of it in state.json. Exactly none of it reaches a pixel. A player can see that heat is 114/133 and six things are frozen, but not which pipe is choking, which of five networks a building is on, or which buildings are dying. The most sophisticated thing in the codebase is invisible.
evidence: tools/check.sh: CHECK GREEN — import, parse, sim lint, 100 tests / 4904 asserts, 4 standalone suites (384+526+129+425 checks), determinism, perf. All pass.
Independent determinism check I ran myself: two processes, first_night, 4000 ticks, state.json sha256 (wall_ms stripped) identical at 1aa43633da3734cb in both. Not taken on trust from the gate.

artifacts/perf.json: stress_1000 → ticks_per_second 45.9, target_ticks_per_second 400.0, floor_ticks_per_second 35.0, ms_per_tick 21.77, status 'slow', overall status 'ok'. 1717 buildings, 1445 heat nodes, tick_hz 20 (50 ms budget). 43% of the tick budget consumed by the four cheapest systems, with logistics, production, citizens, society, threat, combat and research all still unwritten.

artifacts/critic_vis/log.txt: 'frame 135.45 ms | ... | draw 35.99 ms | 206 bld 33 agents 10 lights | 797 draw calls'. draw_us is measured by entity_renderer alone and excludes screenshot capture, so 36 ms of CPU entity drawing for 206 buildings is honest. That is a 27 FPS ceiling before the sim runs, and it projects to roughly 300 ms/frame at the 1717-building stress city. tools/perf.sh is headless, so render cost is entirely ungated.

artifacts/critic_a/log.txt: 'flow repair: 16 cells over 1 field(s) in 27.03 ms'. A single flow-field repair costs more than half the 50 ms tick budget, and repairs fire on building placement — i.e. dragging a line of pipes is a guaranteed hitch.

artifacts/critic_a/metrics.csv, 600 rows x 45 columns: climate.ambient_temp 501 distinct values, heat.delivered 552, heat.total_demand 557, heat.buffer 281 (0.0 to 719.74). The numbers move and correlate with the log. But 7 columns are constant at 0 for all 600 rows.

artifacts/critic_a/state.json (3.6 MB): 208 buildings with per-instance delivered materials, hp, progress, heat_stored; 162 heat nodes with dist/eta/served/flow/bottleneck; 5 networks with bottleneck arrays, brownouts, buffer_capacity, starved counts; climate with a scheduled 'First Frost' on day 3 and 4 queued warnings carrying authored prose; grid terrain zstd-compressed. Rich world state, not scaffolding.

game/sim/heat/heat_flow.gd:401-485 (_fill): the hot loop. _acc Dictionary is cleared and rebuilt, then keys.sort() is executed, INSIDE the `while rounds < MAX_ROUNDS` loop — up to 12 rounds x 3 passes per tier per network per tick. The touched-tile set is the union of _paths[c] over active, which can only shrink between rounds and never changes sort order.

game/sim/heat/heat_flow.gd:510 (_phase_buffers): calls the full _route() on every tick where any demand is unmet and any buffer can discharge, bypassing the cross-tick routing cache. Deficit is nonzero for most of every night in the harness run.
game/core/sim.gd: zero occurrences of get_ticks_usec or any per-system timing. There is no way to attribute the 21.8 ms/tick to a system without adding instrumentation first.

game/play/play_hud.gd is 114 lines and is the entire UI; `ls game/ui/` returns no .gd files. No overlay code exists anywhere (grep for 'overlay' in game/play and world_renderer returns only PlayController.attach's parameter name).
